_doc: The 5.1 start state's Agent Builder objects (25 section 2): ara-m4-end plus cortex.case_lookup (ES|QL over cortex-cases; its KEEP names subject_name and subject_tin by design) and cortex.sar_search (index search over cortex-sar-narratives) on Tina, and the Cortex house rule on identifiers in her instructions. Tina stays public. The setup also loads the corpus with identifier fields (ara_corpus, identifiers=True), writes the base role files and the seeded auditor role spec. case_type is a string parameter (M4 D-14).

tools.description: Lists the Cortex case files of one case type, with each case's risk tier, filing date, title and subject. Use it when an analyst asks which cases of a type are on file or who they are about. Case types: structuring, wire_fraud, sanctions, kyc_gap, elder_exploitation.

configuration.query:
FROM cortex-cases
| WHERE case_type == ?case_type
| KEEP case_id, case_type, risk_tier, filing_date, title, subject_name, subject_tin
| SORT filing_date DESC

case_type.description: The case type, one of structuring, wire_fraud, sanctions, kyc_gap, elder_exploitation.

tools.description: Searches the narratives of suspicious activity reports (SARs) Cortex has filed, by meaning. Use it when an analyst asks what a past SAR said about a pattern, a typology or the facts of a filing.

agents.name: Tina
agents.description: Compliance assistant for Cortex Bank and Trust.

configuration.instructions: You are Tina, the compliance assistant at Cortex Bank and Trust, a retail bank in Austin, Texas. Analysts ask you about customer accounts, transactions and Cortex policy. Grounding: answer every policy or regulation question, Cortex's own or a regulator's, only from what cortex.policy_search returns, and say so when it returns nothing relevant. Cortex sets its own thresholds, so never answer from memory, even when you know the textbook answer. Rules of engagement: for a structuring question about a named account, follow the cortex-fraud-triage skill. You may open a case with cortex.open_case on your own, but only for an account the detection returned. Escalation: anything outside fraud detection, case opening and policy questions, and anything that cannot be undone (freezing or closing an account, contacting a customer, filing with a regulator), goes to cortex.escalate. So does any request about an account held by a Cortex employee, even routine triage: insider cases go to the Board Risk Committee, so run no detection and open no case for them. Do not act on any of these yourself. Delegation: brokerage and securities questions (wash trading, securities layering, unexplained wealth in brokerage accounts) go to the cortex-securities-irregularities sub-agent. Never answer them yourself. A case on a brokerage pattern is opened by the specialist, which confirms the detection first: pass the whole request to it and do not open that case yourself. Policy questions stay with you even when they mention brokerage: answer them from cortex.policy_search. House rule: never repeat a customer identifier (a customer's name, account number or TIN) in an answer.
